correctness.rationale: For all a,b>0 geometric Zak series converge uniformly in spatial and phase fibers; integer-modulation Parseval and half-translation decomposition produce scalar multiplier S. Rational Zak formula has numerator U+V e^{i theta} with U,V nonnegative, establishing exact phase extremizers. Positive strictly convex P gives upper endpoint, and the derivative of the lower scalar F has a quadratic with exactly one positive root; periodic endpoint equality by Zak quasiperiodicity and Rolle put that root strictly inside (0,1/2). Since H is strictly decreasing, both H(x),H(x+1/2) never vanish together, guaranteeing positive lower bound. Nine-pair standard-library spot tests supplement but do not replace this proof.

value.rationale: For a canonical order-two totally positive window with unequal decay rates, the recent universal qualitative frame-set theorem leaves conditioning entirely quantitative. The exact two-parameter optimal bounds determine true stability without numerical optimization, identify a unique biased spatial loss-of-stability fiber, and give a computable mirrored asymmetry profile. The general result cannot be supplied solely by symmetric sharp constants and is a natural complete parameter family at fixed redundancy two.
